# Appendix H — Generated Cursor Artifacts

**What this document covers:** every `.cursor/` artifact generated by the ASDD workflow — rules, skills, hooks, Bugbot config, and notepads. These are produced as side effects of the spec-driven process, not manually authored.

---

## The core idea

The `.cursor/` folder is a **generated artifact** of the workflow, not a static config file. By the time Sprint 1 ships, the project has a complete AI development environment:

- **Rules** encode the standards from the design spec and architecture ADRs — every future code generation session respects them automatically
- **Skills** encode the team's workflows — Red Team, Dead Reckoning, spec compliance, QA test plan generation — reusable on every subsequent feature
- **Hooks** automate quality gates at commit time
- **Bugbot** watches every PR for the exact bug patterns your ADRs identified
- **Notepads** keep project context always available to the AI

Sprint 2 starts with all of this active. **Each feature is cheaper, faster, and more constrained than the last.**

## Rules

### `design-system.mdc` — Generated at Stage 3

**Trigger:** Always on; auto-attached to all `*.tsx`, `*.css` files
**Source:** Design specification (Stage 3)

```markdown
---
description: Rotato design system constraints. Always applied to component and style files.
globs: ["**/*.tsx", "**/*.css"]
alwaysApply: true
---

# Design System Rules

## Colors
- Use ONLY CSS custom properties from globals.css. Never hardcode hex values.
- Available tokens: --color-cream, --color-cream-dark, --color-parchment,
  --color-terracotta, --color-terracotta-light, --color-terracotta-dark,
  --color-sage, --color-sage-light, --color-muted-gold, --color-dusty-blue,
  --color-warm-gray, --color-soft-brown
- For project colors: use values from PALETTE_COLORS in src/lib/constants.ts
- NO red-family colors anywhere (#FF..., #E5..., #DC... ranges).
  Errors use amber/terracotta. Destructive actions use terracotta, not red.

## Typography
- Caveat font: accent text only (section headers, empty states, special labels)
- Inter font: all body text, form labels, buttons, inputs, captions
- Do not mix fonts within a single UI element

## Animations
- Enter transitions: 200–300ms, ease-out
- Exit transitions: 150ms, ease-in
- No abrupt transitions under 150ms for content changes

## Spacing and layout
- Use Tailwind spacing utilities (p-4, gap-2, etc.) — not arbitrary values
- Generous whitespace preferred over dense information layouts

## Accessibility
- All interactive elements need visible focus rings
- Use: outline-2 outline-offset-2 focus:outline-terracotta-light (or equivalent)
- Color is never the sole indicator of state — always pair with icon or text label
- Every form input must have an associated <label>, not just a placeholder
```

---

### `architecture.mdc` — Generated at Stage 4

**Trigger:** Always on; auto-attached to all `*.ts`, `*.tsx` files in `src/`
**Source:** Architecture ADRs (Stage 4)

```markdown
---
description: Rotato architectural constraints derived from ADRs. Always applied to source files.
globs: ["src/**/*.ts", "src/**/*.tsx"]
alwaysApply: true
---

# Architecture Rules (from ADRs)

## State management (ADR-002)
- Use React Context + useReducer ONLY. No Zustand, Redux, Jotai, or other state libraries.
- All state mutations go through GardenAction union types in src/lib/types.ts
- Form field state (ephemeral until submit) may use local useState — this is acceptable

## Persistence (ADR-003)
- All persistence via idb-keyval in src/lib/storage.ts. NO direct localStorage calls.
- Only exception: the onboarding-seen flag uses localStorage (ONBOARDING_KEY constant)

## Hydration guards (ADR-006)
- Any component rendering Date.now(), new Date(), or toLocaleString() in JSX:
  add suppressHydrationWarning to the containing element
- dnd-kit draggable components: wrap in a mounting guard
  const [mounted, setMounted] = useState(false)
  useEffect(() => setMounted(true), [])
  if (!mounted) return <NonDraggableFallback />
- Components that depend on GardenState: check state.hydrated before rendering
  persisted values to avoid flash of empty content

## Constants (do not inline)
- Section metadata: SECTION_META from src/lib/constants.ts
- Section order: SECTION_ORDER from src/lib/constants.ts
- Color palette: PALETTE_COLORS from src/lib/constants.ts
- Icon options: ICON_OPTIONS from src/lib/constants.ts
- Storage key: STORAGE_KEY constant — never use the string "rotato-garden-state" directly

## File structure
- UI primitives: src/components/ui/
- Garden-specific: src/components/garden/
- Form styles: src/components/garden/form-styles/
- Hooks: src/hooks/
- Types: src/lib/types.ts — add all new types here, not inline
```

### `testing-standards.mdc` — Generated at Stage 4

**Trigger:** Auto-attached to `*.test.ts`, `*.test.tsx`, `*.spec.ts` files
**Source:** QA lead standards from architecture review

```markdown
---
description: Rotato testing standards. Applied to all test files.
globs: ["**/*.test.ts", "**/*.test.tsx", "**/*.spec.ts"]
alwaysApply: false
---

# Testing Standards

## Test naming
- Describe: component or function name
- It: "should [behavior] when [condition]"
- Example: it("should preserve field values when style switches", ...)

## Coverage requirements
- Happy path: required for all user-facing interactions
- Edge cases: required for all form submissions (empty, invalid, boundary)
- Regression: any change to GardenContext reducer requires tests for affected actions
- Accessibility: at minimum, test that interactive elements are keyboard reachable

## What not to test
- Implementation details (internal state values, specific class names)
- CSS/visual output — use design-review skill for visual compliance

## Test utilities
- Use React Testing Library, not Enzyme
- Prefer user-event over fireEvent for interaction simulation
- Mock idb-keyval for all tests touching GardenContext persistence
```

## Skills

### `red-team-spec/SKILL.md` — Generated at Stage 2

```markdown
# Red Team My Spec

Run a contradiction and gap audit on any PRD or specification document.

## When to use
Before any architectural or implementation work begins on a new feature or product.
Also use after major spec revisions.

## How to use
Provide the spec as an attachment or paste it. Optionally provide a Confluence page URL
and the agent will fetch it directly.

## What the agent does
Reads the spec and returns a structured audit with three sections:

**CONTRADICTIONS** — statements in the spec that conflict with each other
**MISSING EDGE CASES** — user scenarios not addressed by the spec
**IMPLICIT ASSUMPTIONS** — decisions the spec makes without declaring them

For each finding: exact section cited, risk if unaddressed, minimum fix.

## What the agent does NOT do
Suggest new features. Rewrite the spec. Make product decisions.
It surfaces gaps only.

## Prompt
You are a meticulous product auditor. Your professional reputation depends on
finding the problems a spec doesn't say out loud — the ones that cause rework
six weeks into development.

Read the following specification and return a structured audit with three sections:
CONTRADICTIONS, MISSING EDGE CASES, IMPLICIT ASSUMPTIONS.
For each: cite the exact section, state the risk if unaddressed, and suggest
the minimum addition to the spec that would resolve it.

Do not suggest features. Do not rewrite the spec. Surface gaps only.

Spec: $SPEC
```

### `design-review/SKILL.md` — Generated at Stage 3

```markdown
# Design Review

Check a React component implementation against the Figma design spec.

## When to use
Before opening a PR for any component that has a corresponding Figma frame.
Can also run in CI via the spec-compliance-check skill.

## How to use
Provide the component file and optionally the Figma node URL.

## What the agent does
Compares the component against the Figma spec and the design-system.mdc rule.
Returns a GREEN/AMBER/RED report for:
- Colors (palette tokens vs hardcoded hex)
- Typography (Caveat vs Inter usage)
- Spacing (Tailwind utilities vs arbitrary values)
- Layout structure (column count, order, nesting depth)
- Animation timings
- Accessibility (labels, focus rings, color-only states)

## Prompt
You are a design reviewer checking a React component against its Figma spec
and the Rotato design system rules.

Classify each aspect: GREEN (matches spec), AMBER (acceptable deviation, note it),
RED (violates spec or design-system.mdc rule).

Return a structured report. List all RED items explicitly with the specific fix needed.

Component: $COMPONENT_FILE
Figma spec: $FIGMA_NODE (optional — use design-system.mdc if not provided)
```

### `confidence-map/SKILL.md` — Generated at Stage 4

```markdown
# Confidence Map

Annotate architectural or implementation decisions as GREEN, AMBER, or RED
based on how explicitly they were specified.

## When to use
After writing architecture docs. After completing a feature implementation.
As part of a Tech Lead PR review.

## Classifications
GREEN  — the spec explicitly required or excluded this choice
AMBER  — reasonable default, not contradicted by the spec
RED    — the spec was silent; this decision has downstream consequences

## What RED requires
For every RED item: write the exact question that would have resolved it,
identify the file and line where it has the most impact, and recommend
whether to add it to an ADR or raise it with the PM.

## Prompt
You are a senior architect annotating decisions against a specification.

Given the spec and the list of decisions below, classify each:
GREEN (explicitly specified), AMBER (reasonable default), RED (assumption with consequence).

For every RED: state the exact question that would have resolved it,
and identify which file most depends on this assumption.

Spec: $SPEC
Decisions: $DECISIONS
```

### `tech-lead-review/SKILL.md` — Generated at Stage 4

```markdown
# Tech Lead Review

Review a PR diff against the project's architecture ADRs.

## When to use
As part of the automated review stack before human PR review.
Run after Bugbot, before requesting human review.

## What the agent checks
- Any code that contradicts an accepted ADR
- Direct localStorage calls bypassing idb-keyval (ADR-003)
- State management bypassing GardenContext (ADR-002)
- Missing hydration guards (ADR-006)
- New dependencies not discussed in architecture

## Output
GREEN — no architectural violations found
AMBER — deviations from ADRs that are acceptable; noted for desk check
RED — clear violation of an accepted ADR; must be resolved before merge

## Prompt
You are a Tech Lead reviewing a PR against the project's architectural decisions.

For each changed file in the diff, check for violations of the ADRs listed below.
Return a structured report: GREEN (compliant), AMBER (deviation worth noting),
RED (clear violation — must fix before merge).

For RED items: cite the specific ADR violated and state the required change.

ADRs: $ADR_LIST
PR diff: $PR_DIFF
```

### `dead-reckoning/SKILL.md` — Generated at Stage 5

```markdown
# Dead Reckoning

Read a Jira ticket and surface every implementation decision not answered by the spec
before any code is written.

## When to use
First step for any developer picking up a new ticket. Before the implementation plan.
Before the TDD.

## Classification
LOW STAKES + REVERSIBLE — proceed with the most reasonable default, note the assumption
HIGH STAKES or IRREVERSIBLE — STOP. State the exact question, the options, the downstream
  files affected by each option. Do not continue until this is resolved with PM/Designer/Tech Lead.

## After all STOP items are resolved
The output of this skill becomes the input for the tdd-draft skill.

## Prompt
You are implementing the following Jira ticket. Before writing any code:

1. Read every acceptance criterion completely.
2. List every implementation decision you will need to make that is NOT answered by the spec.
3. Classify each decision:
   - LOW STAKES + REVERSIBLE: proceed with the most reasonable default, note your assumption.
   - HIGH STAKES or IRREVERSIBLE: STOP. State the exact question, the two or three options
     you see, and which downstream files each option affects. Do not continue until resolved.

Only after all STOP items are resolved, confirm you are ready for the TDD draft.

Ticket: $TICKET [Jira MCP]
Architecture doc: $ARCH_DOC [Confluence MCP]
Design spec: $DESIGN_DOC [Confluence MCP]
Existing patterns: [GitHub MCP: search_code $SEARCH_TERM]
```

### `impl-tdd/SKILL.md` — Generated at Stage 6

```markdown
# Implementation TDD

Generate an Implementation TDD from Dead Reckoning resolutions and a Jira ticket.
Documents micro-decisions specific to this ticket's implementation.

## When to use
After all Dead Reckoning STOP items are resolved. Before any code is written.
Tech Lead reviews and approves before implementation begins.

An Implementation TDD written to Confluence, linked to the Jira ticket.
Every Dead Reckoning resolution appears in the Decision Log.

## Prompt
You are a developer writing an Implementation TDD. All ambiguities have been resolved

Write: PROBLEM, APPROACH, ALTERNATIVES CONSIDERED, DECISION LOG, OPEN QUESTIONS (must be empty), CONFIDENCE SUMMARY.

Dead Reckoning resolutions: $RESOLUTIONS
Feature TDD: [Confluence MCP: get_page "Feature TDD: $FEATURE_NAME"]
[Confluence MCP: create_page space="ROT-TDD" title="Impl TDD: $TICKET_ID"]
```

```markdown
# Spec Compliance Check

Run in CI on every PR open. Validates the diff against the linked Jira ticket's
acceptance criteria.

## When to use
Automatically — triggered as a GitHub Action on pull_request event.
Can also be run manually before opening a PR.

## Output
GREEN — diff satisfies this AC
AMBER — diff partially addresses this; manual verification needed
RED   — this AC is not addressed by the diff

If any RED: output "SPEC-INCOMPLETE" and list the exact ACs. The PR is blocked
from human review until RED items are resolved or explicitly waived.

## Prompt
You are a spec compliance auditor in a CI pipeline.

Compare the PR diff against every acceptance criterion in the linked Jira ticket.
Classify each AC: GREEN (satisfied), AMBER (partial), RED (not addressed).

If any RED items exist, output "SPEC-INCOMPLETE" followed by the exact ACs missing.

Ticket: $TICKET_ID [Jira MCP: get_issue]
PR diff: $PR_NUMBER [GitHub MCP: list_pull_request_files]
```

### `update-adr/SKILL.md` — Generated at Stage 10

```markdown
# Update ADR

Post-merge: compare the merged code against existing ADRs in Confluence.
Draft superseding ADR entries where code diverged from accepted decisions.

## When to use
Automatically after every merge to main. Keeps architecture docs current
without manual maintenance.

## What the agent does
1. Reads all ADRs from Confluence ROT-ARCH space
2. Reads the merged diff from GitHub
3. For each ADR: checks whether the merged code is consistent with the decision
4. Where code diverges: drafts a "supersedes ADR-00X" page with:
   - What changed
   - Why (from commit message and TDD if available)
   - New status (Superseded or Amended)
   - Consequences of the change

## Prompt
You are a Tech Lead maintaining living architecture documentation.

Compare the merged PR diff against all existing ADRs. For each ADR that the
merged code contradicts or extends: draft a superseding or amending ADR entry.

Use Nygard format: Status (Superseded/Amended), Context, Decision, Consequences.

Existing ADRs: [Confluence MCP: search_pages space="ROT-ARCH" label="adr"]
Merged diff: [GitHub MCP: get_pull_request $PR_NUMBER files]
```

## `bugbot.json` — Generated at Stage 8

Bugbot configuration derived from the architecture ADRs. Tells Bugbot exactly which patterns to flag in this codebase — not generic lint rules, but project-specific risks identified during architecture review.

```json
{
  "enabled": true,
  "reviewOn": ["pull_request"],
  "focus": [
    {
      "pattern": "localStorage\\.getItem|localStorage\\.setItem|localStorage\\.removeItem",
      "exclude": ["ONBOARDING_KEY"],
      "message": "Direct localStorage call detected. Use idb-keyval via src/lib/storage.ts (ADR-003).",
      "severity": "warning"
    },
    {
      "pattern": "Date\\.now\\(\\)|new Date\\(\\)|toLocaleString\\(\\)",
      "context": "jsx",
      "message": "Dynamic date/time in JSX without suppressHydrationWarning. Add suppressHydrationWarning to the containing element (ADR-006).",
      "severity": "error"
    },
    {
      "pattern": "useSortable|DraggableItem",
      "requiresPattern": "useState.*mounted|mounted.*useState",
      "message": "dnd-kit draggable component may be missing client-side mounting guard, causing hydration mismatch (ADR-004, ADR-006).",
      "severity": "error"
    },
    {
      "pattern": "#[0-9A-Fa-f]{3,6}",
      "context": "tsx",
      "exclude": ["PALETTE_COLORS", "SECTION_COLORS", "globals.css"],
      "message": "Hardcoded hex color detected. Use CSS custom properties from globals.css or constants from src/lib/constants.ts.",
      "severity": "warning"
    },
    {
      "pattern": "import.*zustand|import.*redux|import.*jotai",
      "message": "External state library detected. Use React Context + useReducer (ADR-002).",
      "severity": "error"
    }
  ]
}
```

## Notepad: `project-context`

Created at Stage 1. Attached to every Cursor AI session in this project.

```
# Rotato — Project Context

## Problem
Creatives have too many projects and no low-pressure way to manage them.
Existing tools create anxiety (task managers) or no structure (note apps).

## Anti-urgency constraint
This is the core design principle. No deadlines, no completion percentages,
no streaks. Everything in the UI should feel permissive and calm.

## Personas
- Multidisciplinary Maker: 8–15 projects across domains
- Hobby Juggler: seasonal creative work
- Creative Burnout Recoverer: actively avoids productivity software

## Sections (fixed)
- Currently Playing: active, excited about now
- Resting: dormant but not abandoned
- Seeds: undeveloped ideas
- Finished Worlds: completed or retired

## Architecture constraints (summary — see architecture.mdc for full rules)
- Local-first: idb-keyval only. No backend. No account system. Ever.
- State: React Context + useReducer (GardenContext)
- SSR: Next.js App Router — hydration guards required for Date and dnd-kit

## What NOT to suggest
- Deadline or due date fields
- User accounts or sync
- Collaboration features
- Gamification (streaks, percentages, badges)
- Red colors anywhere in the UI
```
